geo_headlines: IRAN: TWO-DAY HORMUZ PLAN. **Iran's foreign minister said talks with Qatari mediators cut the timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz from five days to two, if the US meets Iran's conditions, including sanctions relief and the release of frozen funds; he said no direct talks with US officials are scheduled (Dawn, SBS).** Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha Saturday after more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran Friday (Reuters via GMA).

WASHINGTON: NO DECISION YET. Secretary of State Rubio said Saturday that Trump has not decided on new strikes and would prefer a diplomatic outcome (Reuters via GMA). Trump said talks are going fine and he is in no hurry, but that the US still has to take care of one or two targets, including the suspected Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site, which he said could be done in 10 minutes (Arab News). Reports say Gulf allies were told strikes could come as early as November 4 (Times of Israel).

TEHRAN: HARDER WARNINGS. Iran's supreme leader ordered the armed forces to answer any attack immediately and without geographic limits and to update target lists (Dawn). Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran is debating whether to lift its ban on nuclear weapons if fighting resumes, though no decision has been taken (Reuters via GMA). He also said the tone of a US letter from Vice President Vance has completely changed (AP via Sun Sentinel).

HORMUZ TRAFFIC. Iranian state television reported a ship hit a mine and caught fire in the strait Saturday (Daily Star). A tracker counted 41 crossings in the 24 hours to early Sunday (Hormuz tracker). Brent and WTI have not traded since Friday's settles of $113.10 and $104.12; futures reopen 6 PM ET.

FRIDAY RECAP. S&P 500 -1.82% to 7,580.07, Nasdaq Composite -2.86% (its biggest drop since June 5), chips -7.2% after Intel's 28.6% drop (Reuters). For the week the S&P fell 0.57% and sits 3.05% below its October 6 record close. Gold $3,898.90, 10-year 4.94%, VIX 19.42.

THIS WEEK. Monday: ISM manufacturing 10:00 AM; Apple (call 5:00 PM) and Palantir after the close. Tuesday: midterm elections; JOLTS 10:00 AM; AMD. Wednesday: ADP 8:15 AM, ISM services 10:00 AM. Friday: October payrolls 8:30 AM, consensus about +65,000 after September's +29,000 (CNBC, ThriveInMarkets). Clocks fell back overnight; futures reopen 6 PM ET.
client_frame_short: The weekend tilted slightly toward diplomacy, but both paths stay open. Iran says a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days is on the table if its conditions are met, and Washington says no strike decision has been made. **At the same time, reports still point to possible US strikes as early as Wednesday, and Iran's leadership is issuing harder warnings, so oil can swing either way when futures reopen Sunday evening.** For clients: this is a week of headlines (Iran, the midterms, Apple, and the jobs report). Stay diversified and keep to the plan.
client_frame:
If a client calls this weekend, the honest answer is that the next few days could move markets in either direction, and that is exactly why we do not trade on headlines.

What changed: Iran's foreign minister said Qatari mediation shortened its plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz from five days to two, provided the US meets conditions such as sanctions relief and releasing frozen funds. Secretary of State Rubio said President Trump has not decided on new strikes and prefers diplomacy. Trump said talks are going fine but that one or two targets, including a suspected nuclear site, remain. Iran's supreme leader ordered the military to respond to any attack without geographic limits.

Where we stand: on Friday the S&P 500 fell 1.8% and the Nasdaq 2.9% on Intel and Amazon. For the week the S&P fell about 0.6% and is about 3% below its October 6 record close. Brent settled at $113.10 and gold at $3,898.90. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.94%.

The week ahead: Apple and Palantir report Monday, the midterm elections are Tuesday, and the October jobs report is Friday, with economists expecting about 65,000 new jobs after just 29,000 in September. Reports say strikes could come as early as Wednesday.

Why it matters: a credible Hormuz reopening would likely pull oil sharply lower and ease inflation and rate-hike fears; renewed strikes would push oil higher and add to inflation worries. A diversified portfolio is built to live through both outcomes without needing to guess which one comes first, or when.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and avoid making election-week or Iran-headline trades in either direction. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Friday 4.94%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Friday 5.31%), or US strikes that keep Brent well above $105 (Friday $113.10).
